blogs.title: When the MRI Is Normal: Diagnosing Acute Neuro-Behçet’s Without a Lesion
blogs.description: This post would explore the diagnostic challenge of acute neuro-Behçet’s disease presenting with headache, vertigo, fever, and CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis despite a normal brain MRI. It would emphasize that early neuro-Behçet’s may manifest as aseptic meningitis without parenchymal lesions, and discuss how clinicians should integrate mucocutaneous findings, CSF data, and exclusion of infection rather than over-relying on neuroimaging.

blogs.title: Hyponatremia With a Rash and a Headache: SIADH as a Clue to CNS Inflammation
blogs.description: This post would focus on SIADH as a potentially underrecognized complication of acute neuro-Behçet’s disease. It would review the bedside and laboratory approach to hypo-osmolar euvolemic hyponatremia, discuss how CNS inflammation can trigger inappropriate ADH release, and consider whether inflammatory mediators such as IL-6 may link neuroinflammation and sodium derangements in systemic inflammatory disease.

blogs.title: The Behçet’s Diagnosis That Declares Itself Late: Why the Genital Ulcer Changed Everything
blogs.description: This piece would examine the evolving diagnosis of Behçet’s disease in a patient who initially had nonspecific systemic symptoms and oral aphthae, but only later developed the more specific genital ulcer that clarified the syndrome. It would highlight the importance of serial examination, the practical use of the International Criteria for Behçet’s Disease, and the pitfalls of anchoring too early on infection or nonspecific inflammatory syndromes.

blogs.title: Broad Differential, Narrow Signal: Testing Discipline in Aseptic Meningitis With Systemic Inflammation
blogs.description: This blog would analyze the tension between appropriately broad early workup and low-value indiscriminate testing in patients with fever, headache, hyponatremia, and inflammatory markers. Using this case, it would discuss empiric antimicrobials, CSF-driven exclusion of infectious causes, and the limited interpretability of screening tests such as ACE and mildly elevated sIL-2R when pretest probability for sarcoidosis or lymphoma is low.

blogs.title: Hiccups, CK Elevation, and Sodium 124: The Odd Clues of Clinically Important Hyponatremia
blogs.description: This post would use the case to teach the less appreciated manifestations of significant hyponatremia, including persistent hiccups and rhabdomyolysis. It would review how these findings can be missed or attributed to unrelated illness, why CK may be worth checking in selected hyponatremic patients with malaise or myalgias, and how careful sodium correction remains central even when the underlying driver is inflammatory CNS disease.

blogs.title: Colchicine Instead of Steroids? Reconsidering Treatment Thresholds in Mild Acute Neuro-Behçet’s
blogs.description: This article would examine the management implications of apparent improvement of acute neuro-Behçet’s and SIADH with colchicine monotherapy and fluid restriction, without corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants. It would discuss how this case fits uneasily with standard teaching that steroids are the mainstay of acute neuro-Behçet’s treatment, and explore whether selected patients with milder meningeal presentations might be managed more conservatively while acknowledging the limits of single-case inference.
